audit.summary: Two bounded Problems: displayed XD-Violence averages and comparative prose are inconsistent; the literal normal-similarity-minus-one alternative score reverses the intended anomaly ordering. The displayed fine-grained average ranking survives arithmetic correction. Core implementation and explanation claims retain unresolved evidence requirements.
limitations: P1 — Reported averages and comparative statements are internally inconsistent — Counterevidence: Recomputed Ex-VAD averages still lead both fine-grained tables. Hidden precision can explain Table5 caption10.874 vs10.88 and STPrompt23.448 vs23.44; neither is counted as error. The paper acknowledges second-best coarse XD AP and the TCVADS comparison elsewhere. No historical ranking reversal is demonstrated.

P2 — The written normal-similarity rule reverses anomaly ordering — Counterevidence: A wording reversal is plausible. The separate direct classifier branch remains available, and the paper selects between branches. No implementation or trained predictions are supplied, so the deployed formula and any published score effect are unresolved.
Limitations: No verified author repository or code archive is staged; this is an access/discovery limitation, not proof of global nonrelease.
Limitations: Raw predictions, run identifiers, exact prompts, trained parameter graph, selection splits and authoritative table outputs are unavailable.
Limitations: Historical implementation of the normal-similarity rule, fusion mappings and trainable label pathway cannot be resolved from the supplied PDF alone.
Limitations: Explanation factuality/faithfulness and full end-to-end cost require additional evaluation artifacts; no empirical reproduction was performed.
Limitations: Optional OpenReview metadata and possible separate-supplement endpoint returned HTTP403 during source preparation; attachment existence and later revisions/errata are unresolved.
Limitations: Baseline studies were not independently retrieved; comparisons use the paper's reported values. Citation mismatches alone were not promoted to scientific Problems.
Limitations: No author-code execution, model inference, dataset/weight download, software installation, external API call, replacement benchmark or validated full repaired pipeline.
The original report's complete scope, counterevidence and unresolved questions are retained below.
This import checks publication format and identity; it does not repeat scientific review.
Independent human scientific review is pending; author adoption has not been requested.

proposition.claim:
AVG is the mean mAP over the five stated IoU thresholds; tables and Section4.2 describe the same comparisons.

Section3.6 describes an alternative anomaly score as similarity to the normal class minus1, while Equation7 and Figure5 use high scores for anomalies.
proposition.domain: Completed report for I25-43589; exact inspected scope and limitations are retained in the report and coverage ledger.
assumptions: Five components receive equal weight under the stated AVG definition.
Reported components and averages are rounded to two decimal places; combined discrepancy allowance is 0.010 percentage points.
No new benchmark scores or unobserved runs are inferred.
Normal and anomalous class embeddings are nonzero unit vectors LN=(1,0), LA=(-1,0).
Fused normal and anomalous frames are LN and LA, respectively; they are admitted vectors of the written cosine-score rule, not asserted historical CLIP outputs.
Equation10 class penalty is zero for these class embeddings, because their cosine is -1.
Anomaly is the positive class; larger scores indicate anomaly; repeated copies support any valid topK.
